subject: RFI: SLA metrics, measurement & crediting approach
messages:
From: Danielle Price <danielle.price@acme-enterprises.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@acme-enterprises.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T15:22:00Z
Subject: RFI: SLA measurement and credit policy (initial questions)

Marcus —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier. Acme is collecting detailed answers for the RFI and we need clarity on how Redwood measures uptime/latency, and how service credits are calculated and issued. High level items we need documented:

- Exact definition of "availability" (per region/az/service)
- Measurement sources (customer-visible probes vs. internal telemetry)
- Aggregation windows and percentiles used for latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99)
- Maintenance windows and scheduled downtime treatment
- Exclusions (force majeure, customer configuration, DDoS mitigation)
- Credit calculation formula and monthly cap
- Evidence package required to validate a claim
- Typical timeline from claim to credit application

Can you respond with a short write-up or attach your measurement methodology? We included a template spreadsheet for credits in the RFI packet (attached).

Thanks,
Danielle
Procurement Manager — Acme Enterprises
From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: Danielle Price <danielle.price@acme-enterprises.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-02T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: SLA measurement and credit policy (initial questions)

Danielle —

Appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a concise response and attached our SLA Measurement Methodology PDF and the Monthly Service Credit form pre-filled with our standard language. High-level answers below; attaching the PDF for the detailed breakdown.

1) Availability definition
- "Availability" is the percentage of successful inference requests (HTTP 2xx) served by a given model endpoint in a region, measured from the customer-visible API ingress (edge) across the Redwood control plane and serving runtime. For multi-AZ customers we report both per-region and aggregated multi-AZ availability.

2) Measurement sources
- Primary: synthetic probes executed from third-party vantage points (publicly routable probes) that replicate customer API calls to the configured endpoint and record success/failure and latency.
- Secondary: production telemetry (edge LB metrics + backend per-instance response codes) used for root-cause analysis and internal validation.

3) Aggregation windows and latency percentiles
- Uptime SLA is a rolling 30-day window (UTC).
- Latency commitments are provided as p95 and p99 percentiles over a 24-hour aggregation for eligibility checks; monthly reporting uses daily p95/p99 aggregated to a month. Example: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 800ms for our standard low-latency tier (specific numbers vary by model class).

4) Maintenance windows and scheduled downtime
- Planned maintenance is scheduled at least 72 hours in advance and announced via the Console + email. Planned downtime under announced windows is excluded from SLA calculations if application follows the announced routing guidance.

5) Exclusions
- Exclusions include customer misconfiguration (network/VPC rules, credentials), force majeure, DDoS events where mitigation changes request routing, and incidents where a customer-selected private deployment has a 3rd-party-managed network outage.

6) Credit calculation and caps
- Standard credit: For each 30-day rolling period, if availability falls below the SLA threshold, credit = (SLA shortfall %) * (monthly invoice for Redwood-hosted inference). Example: SLA = 99.9%, observed = 99.5% -> shortfall 0.4% -> credit = 0.4% * invoice.
- Latency breach credit: Separate credit schedule for latency breaches using a fixed bucket table (e.g., p99 > target by X -> Y% credit).
- Cap: Total credits per month are capped at 50% of the Redwood portion of the invoice.

7) Evidence required
- Customer must submit a claim within 30 days of the end of the affected period including:
  - Time window(s) of impact (UTC)
  - Synthetic probe IDs or request IDs from their side, if available
  - Any Console/exported CSVs showing errors/latency
- Redwood will respond with internal validation artifacts (aggregated probe results, edge request logs, and per-instance traces) and a joint reconciliation table. Credits are issued only after mutual validation.

8) Timeline
- Acknowledgement within 3 business days, preliminary validation within 10 business days, final determination and credit applied on next invoice cycle (or issued as one-off credit within 30 days of agreement).

I've copied Marissa (Customer Success lead) and Karthik (Legal/Product) to help with any contract language edits. Full method and sampling details are in the PDF. Let me know which model class and region you want us to run a pre-RFI audit against so we can provide precomputed measurements.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Quick practical note on evidence: for faster turnaround we recommend customers enable request tracing and share a 48-hour window of request IDs (we provide an export tool in Console). That allows us to reconcile sampled production traces with synthetic probe data and reduce the validation window from 10 to 5 business days in many cases.

If Acme can provide a short list of critical endpoints (model names + routes) we will generate a two-week sample report and include p95/p99 baselines. Would you be able to identify 3 routes you care most about?

Thanks,

- For credit adjudication, what is the appeals process if our internal metrics show a different picture?

Attaching the RFI spreadsheet we referenced — you'll see the SRE fields.

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-06T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: SLA measurement and crediting approach

Oliver —

Answers inline to the SRE questions: 

- Probe vantage lists: We will provide an anonymized list of dataplane egress CIDR blocks and geographic regions (US: us-east-1, us-west-2; EU: eu-west-1; APAC: ap-southeast-1) and allow Acme to run validation tests from their infra when signing an NDA. Probe cadence: default 30s for critical endpoints; configurable down to 10s for dedicated customers.

- Multi-AZ weighting: Availability is computed at the region level as the simple ratio of successful requests / total requests across all AZs in that region (i.e., region-level aggregation). We report per-AZ metrics separately. If one AZ is down but the region remains healthy due to routing, the region-level SLA reflects the combined traffic. For customers who require strict per-AZ guarantees we offer dedicated capacity profiles with per-AZ SLOs (contractual add-on).

- Appeals process: If Acme's internal metrics disagree with Redwood's findings, submit a formal claim with the exported traces and probe IDs. We open a cross-functional investigation (SRE/Product/Legal) and run a reprocessing job of the raw events within a mutually agreed time window. If a discrepancy persists, we escalate to the legal review board for final reconciliation. Our goal is transparent evidence and joint reconciliation; credits are not unilateral and require validation.

If this sounds acceptable we'll add the detailed probe IP ranges and cadence table to the PDF and re-share.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product & Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
